affected_system: non-clinical emergency call handling, unit readiness, and incident support network
alternatives: activate a bounded reserve from forecast risk bands for emergency call and unit-hour demand
use rolling forecasts and conservative capacity triggers for emergency call and unit-hour demand
pair spatiotemporal incident and service-time forecasting with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Calls, incidents, dispositions, unit states, travel, scene time, and outcomes remain distinct.
Any operational recommendation requires agency safety review and cannot automate high-stakes dispatch.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: continue ordinary capacity planning for emergency call and unit-hour demand.

constraints.description: The emergency response readiness and allocation forecast must respect declared validated operational capacity and forecast uncertainty.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: emergency communications director and public-safety operations chief
decision_question: What place-time priority call, unit-hour, and mutual-aid demand range should readiness planning use?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The emergency response readiness and allocation forecast must respect declared validated operational capacity and forecast uncertainty.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for emergency call and unit-hour demand passes documented checks for held-out error, interval coverage, event detection, drift, and baseline comparison.

intended_claim: A versioned forecast design for comparing declared alternatives affecting emergency call and unit-hour demand, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: distributional gap in priority unit-hours above deployable capacity
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not present forecast calls as incidents, casualties, or verified emergency need.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for emergency call and unit-hour demand passes documented checks for held-out error, interval coverage, event detection, drift, and baseline comparison.

title: Forecast emergency call and unit demand
transportability_risks: Call coding, dispatch policy, mutual aid, geography, traffic, staffing, and incident mix differ.
Recorded response time may omit call processing, staging, or outcome quality.
